sentenceSets.sentence: Her partiality toward the established approach was understandable but made her assessment of the new one less useful than it might have been.

answerChoices.reasoning: Deference is yielding to someone else's authority, but the sentence describes a leaning of her own that colored her judgment, with no superior in the picture to defer to.
Loyalty is an obligation owed to a person or institution, whereas the sentence is about how her own inclination distorted her evaluation of a competing method.
Sympathy toward an approach would be a harmless attitude, and the sentence identifies something that actively degraded the value of her assessment.
Receptivity is an openness to what comes, which would have improved rather than damaged her reading of a new approach.
Nostalgia is longing for a vanished past, but the established approach is still in use and is the standard against which she measures the newcomer.
Familiarity is just knowing something well, and knowing a method well would not by itself make an assessment less useful.
Enthusiasm describes energy for a subject rather than a tilt between two rivals, and the sentence's concern is comparative judgment.
Expertise would be an asset in evaluating a new method, which contradicts the sentence's claim that the quality named diminished her usefulness.
Hostility toward the established approach would have pushed her judgment the other way, not toward defending it.
An even hand is precisely what the sentence says was missing when she assessed the newer approach.
Detachment implies no stake at all, which would remove the very thing the sentence calls understandable in her.

sentenceSets.sentence: He had a lifelong partiality for cheap detective novels and kept a leaning stack of them on the floor beside his bed.

answerChoices.reasoning: Obsession implies the books ruled him, but the sentence shows a modest stack kept within reach at bedtime, a comfortable habit rather than a compulsion.
Reverence would mean he held the novels in high esteem, and he is described as keeping cheap paperbacks in an untidy pile on the floor.
Tolerance means putting up with something you would rather avoid, yet he deliberately keeps a supply of these books at his bedside for years.
Curiosity suggests he was investigating the genre, but a lifelong stack by the bed points to steady pleasure rather than inquiry.
Aptitude concerns what someone is good at, and nothing in the sentence has him writing or analyzing anything, only reading for his own sake.
Susceptibility implies he was helplessly worked on by the books, while the sentence presents a chosen and comfortable habit.
Admiration would sit awkwardly with novels the sentence pointedly calls cheap, and stacking them on the floor is not the treatment given to prized things.
Indulgence names an occasional treat one grants oneself, whereas this is described as lasting his whole life and furnished permanently beside the bed.
Someone averse to these books would not keep a stack of them within arm's reach of his pillow.
Contempt cannot be squared with a lifelong habit of keeping the novels at hand for reading.
Disdain would mean he looked down on the books, which is contradicted by his keeping a fresh supply at his bedside for decades.

sentenceSets.sentence: Defense counsel moved to disqualify the judge, citing a partiality that three earlier rulings in the same matter had made difficult to ignore.

answerChoices.reasoning: Animus means personal ill will toward a party, but a pattern of rulings leaning one way shows a tilt in the judge's judgment without proving any hostility behind it.
A vendetta is a sustained campaign of revenge, and the only evidence offered is three rulings issued in the ordinary course of the case.
Impropriety names conduct that breaks the rules, whereas issuing rulings is exactly what a judge is authorized to do; the objection is to which way they went.
Caprice means unpredictable whim, but three rulings that all lean the same direction form a consistent pattern rather than a random one.
Negligence would mean the judge was careless, and the motion rests on the direction of the rulings rather than on any failure of attention.
Incompetence is an inability to do the job at all, which nothing about three coherent rulings in one matter suggests.
An irregularity is a procedural defect, while the cited basis is the substance of decisions the judge had full authority to make.
Inconsistency would require the rulings to conflict with one another, but they are cited together as reinforcing a single point.
Nobody moves to disqualify a judge for being even-handed, and the rulings are offered as grounds for removal.
Rigor is a virtue in a judge and could not support a motion to take the case away from one.
Clemency concerns leniency in punishment, which has nothing to do with why counsel wants this judge removed from the matter.
